evals.name: commit-split-trunk-pr-update
evals.prompt: Don't run anything, just write the plan. Our repo's default branch is `trunk`. I'm on trunk with three unrelated uncommitted changes: (1) src/paginate.js: fixed an off-by-one that dropped the last item of every page; (2) src/export.js: added a new toCsv() export; (3) src/util.js: ran prettier, whitespace only. Write commit-plan.md with the exact git commands to put this work on a new branch, the branch name, and the full commit messages. I'll push the branch right away so a teammate can follow along, and trunk will have moved on by the time I open the PR, so also give the exact commands to bring the branch up to date right before opening the PR. Do not ask questions; state assumptions in the file.
evals.expected_output: Three atomic conventional commits on a <type>/<desc> branch off trunk, files staged individually, then a merge (not rebase) of trunk into the pushed branch before the PR, no force-push, no main/master.
expectations: commit-plan.md uses trunk as the base and never names main or master as a branch
No force push anywhere in commit-plan.md
No rebase command in commit-plan.md (the branch is already pushed and shared)
Three separate commits, one per change, with the util.js prettier reformat in its own commit and not mixed with logic
Each file is staged explicitly (e.g. git add src/paginate.js) rather than git add -A / git add . / git commit -a
Conventional commit subjects with correct types: fix for paginate, feat for toCsv, style (or chore) for util.js; imperative mood and under 72 characters
Branch name follows <type>/<short-description> (e.g. feat/csv-export or fix/paginate-off-by-one) and is created from trunk

Pre-PR update merges trunk into the branch (git fetch then git merge origin/trunk, or git pull origin trunk without --rebase) rather than rebasing, and explains that this keeps pushed commit SHAs and avoids a force-push

scripted_checks.text: commit-plan.md uses trunk as the base and never names main or master as a branch
scripted_checks.check: test -s commit-plan.md && grep -q trunk commit-plan.md && ! grep -qE '(origin/|checkout +|switch +|merge +|from +)(main|master)\b' commit-plan.md

scripted_checks.text: No force push anywhere in commit-plan.md
No rebase command in commit-plan.md (the branch is already pushed and shared)

evals.name: pickaxe-restore-mainline
evals.prompt: Don't run anything, just write the plan. Our default branch is `mainline`. Tenant checks silently stopped working: somebody removed the `validateTenant(req);` call from src/auth.js somewhere in the last ~200 commits. I also have unrelated uncommitted edits in src/paginate.js and src/util.js that must stay uncommitted. Write investigation.md with: the exact git commands to find the commit that removed the call and confirm it; the exact commands to restore the call as a reviewable fix on its own branch, with the branch name and full commit message; and how to keep that pushed branch current with mainline while the PR waits for review. Do not ask questions; state assumptions in the file.
evals.expected_output: git log -S finds the removing commit, git show confirms, a single fix(auth) commit on a fix/<desc> branch off mainline with only src/auth.js, other edits left uncommitted, branch kept current by merging mainline, no force-push or rebase.
expectations: investigation.md uses mainline and never names main or master as a branch
No force push anywhere in investigation.md
Uses a pickaxe search (git log -S or -G) for validateTenant
No rebase command in investigation.md (keeping a pushed branch current)
Confirms the found commit with git show (or equivalent) before acting on it
Fix goes on a fix/<short-description> branch created from mainline
Fix commit touches only src/auth.js: stages it explicitly and leaves src/paginate.js and src/util.js uncommitted (no git add -A / commit -a; a stash that is popped afterward is fine)
Commit subject is conventional with type fix and an auth scope (fix(auth): ...), imperative, under 72 characters
Keeps the pushed branch current by merging mainline into it (fetch + merge origin/mainline), not by rebasing, so pushed SHAs are preserved and no force-push is needed

scripted_checks.text: investigation.md uses mainline and never names main or master as a branch
scripted_checks.check: test -s investigation.md && grep -q mainline investigation.md && ! grep -qE '(origin/|checkout +|switch +|merge +|from +)(main|master)\b' investigation.md

scripted_checks.text: No force push anywhere in investigation.md
Uses a pickaxe search (git log -S or -G) for validateTenant
No rebase command in investigation.md (keeping a pushed branch current)
